q: Board costs $£36.88$ per pack of $50$ A2 sheets ($420 \times 594\ \text{mm}$). You need $310\ \text{m}^2$ of board, and can only buy whole packs. What is the total cost?
qShort: $£36.88$ per pack of $50$ A2 · need $310\ \text{m}^2$ · total cost?

lines.say: Packaging board comes in packs of fifty A2 sheets, at thirty-six pounds eighty-eight a pack. {need}You need three hundred and ten square metres. What does the order cost?
This is a real Edexcel A-level D and T question. Pause and have a go!
Okay! One A2 sheet is {sheet}four twenty by five nine four millimetres. {m}In metres, that's nought point four two by nought point five nine four, {a}which is just under a quarter of a square metre.
{pack}Fifty sheets per pack, so one pack covers twelve point four seven four square metres.
{n}Three hundred and ten, divided by that, is twenty-four point eight five packs.
But you can only buy whole packs! {up}So round up to twenty-five.
Twenty-five times thirty-six eighty-eight {ans}is nine hundred and twenty-two pounds!
If you got nine sixteen fifty-three, {trap}you paid for nought point eight five of a pack. Shops don't sell that!
